column3: One of the six great monasteries of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism and the birthplace of its founder, Tsongkhapa. It is known for its butter sculptures, murals and appliqué art.
One of the largest mosques in northwest China, in Xining, with a grand hall that holds thousands of worshippers.
A museum of the plateau, with Tibetan art, ancient pottery and displays about the wildlife and peoples of Qinghai.
A busy food lane in Xining, with stalls of noodles, yogurt, mutton and sweets, where locals shop and eat.
Plain boiled mutton on the bone, eaten with salt or a chili dip, a hearty staple of the plateau.
A cool, springy noodle dish with chili oil, vinegar and sesame, which is especially refreshing in summer.
A wine made from highland barley, a drink at Tibetan festivals and gatherings, light and slightly sweet.
Thick yogurt made from yak or cow milk, tangy and rich, eaten with sugar on the plateau.
Roasted barley flour mixed with butter tea and kneaded by hand, a staple for Tibetan herders on the high plateau.
A flaky pancake whose odd name makes visitors laugh. It is a popular local bread, which is fried until golden and soft.
Yak meat is lean and rich, and is boiled, stewed or dried into jerky, a staple of the high plateau.
Hua'er are folk songs sung in the open air by Han, Hui, Tu and other peoples, with free, high-pitched voices.
Regong art is a tradition of Tibetan Buddhist painting and sculpture, with thangka paintings made by artists in the area of Tongren.
China's largest lake, a vast, deep-blue salt lake high on the plateau. Fields of yellow rapeseed flowers bloom around it in summer, and many birds gather here.
A long range with snow peaks, glaciers and meadows on the edge of the plateau, with herds of yaks and sheep.
A hill of red rock in the Qilian foothills, which offers views over the green valley and the river below.
A scaleless carp that lives in Qinghai Lake and swims up rivers to spawn, a slow-growing fish that is now protected.
Honey from the bees that gather nectar from the vast fields of rapeseed flowers in Menyuan.
An international road cycling race around Qinghai Lake, held each summer, that draws riders from many countries.
A Ming-era temple with fine murals and a palace-like hall, sometimes called the Little Forbidden City of Qinghai.
A Neolithic site where a disaster, perhaps a flood and earthquake, froze a village in time. A bowl of 4,000-year-old noodles was found here.
A coiled embroidery of the Tu people, in which the threads are twisted and coiled into bright patterns on cloth.
A shallow salt lake that mirrors the sky like a giant mirror. When the water is still, the clouds seem to float below your feet.
A lake of salt crystals in the Qaidam Basin, where mineral colors turn the water green and blue.
Goji berries from the Qaidam Basin, grown in salty soil under strong sun, are dark red and sweet.
Salt harvested from the vast Qarhan Salt Lake, which is so hard that a road and a railway are built on it.
A monastery in Yushu with prayer flags and mani stones, an important center for Tibetan Buddhism.
Caterpillar fungus is gathered in the high meadows in spring and is prized in traditional medicine.
A summer festival where horse riders race and show their skills while families camp in tents on the grassland.
A large monastery in Tongren with fine paintings, sculptures and a long tradition of Tibetan art.
Sculptures made of colored butter, shaped into flowers and figures for festivals, which melt away after the show.
A sacred snow range that Tibetans believe is home to a powerful mountain god, and which pilgrims circle on foot.
A sweet pear grown in the warm Yellow River valley at Guide, among the best fruits of the Qinghai plateau.
